To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HSP60 and 70 specific proinflammatory and cytotoxic response of CD4+ CD28 null cells are associated with chronic kidney disease.

the expansion of CD4+ CD28null cells in chronic kidney disease (CD4+CD28 null cells are expanded in the peripheral blood of patients in chronic kidney disease and associate with subclinical atheroclerosis) is triggered by the heat shock proteins (HSP)60 and 70, which are released from the damaged kidney cells.

CD4+ CD28null T cells, which are expanded in patients with chronic kidney diseases (CKD), are activated and proliferate in response to heat shock proteins (HSPs) and this activation is associated with the expression of proinflammatory and cytotoxic molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms that lead to the development of atherosclerosis and cardiovascular disease in patients with CKD.
the study of the role played by CD4+CD281null cells in the pathogenesis of chronic kidney disease.
the identification and characterization of a new subset of CD4+ T cells, the CD4+ CD28null subset, in chronic kidney disease (stage V-IV) and healthy subjects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expansion and activation of CD4+ T cells with CD28 null phenotype in patients with chronic kidney diseases is triggered by the exposure of these cells to heat shock proteins 60 and 7
CD4+ CD28 null T cells are expanded and activated in patients with CKD and are associated with increased risk for cardiovascular events.
the HSP60 and 70 specific proinflammatory and cytotoxic response of CD4+ CD28null cells is a key feature of chronic kidney disease and is associated with subclinical vascular disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HSP60 and 70 induce the expression of IFNy, perforin, granzyme B, and TNFa by the CD4+ CD28null cells in chronic kidney disease (Figure 1).
the expansion and activation of CD4+ CD28null cells in chronic kidney disease (stage IV-V) is associated with the increased expression of heat shock proteins in the peripheral blood.
the expansion of the CD4+ CD28null cells in CKD patients may be triggered by HSP60 and/or HSP70, which are released from injured cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD4+28null cells in patients with CKD react to HSP60 and 70 and this reaction is associated with the expression of proinflammatory and cytotoxic molecules, such as perforin and granyzme B.
CD4+ CD28null cells are expanded in CKD patients and they have an inflammatory response to HSP60 and 70.
CD4+28null cells in CKD subjects are activated by HSP60 and 70 and this may be a trigger for the expansion of this cell population in these patients.
